newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse approves 7-Eleven warrants issue.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse approves 7-Eleven warrants issue.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange had approved warrants with non-detachable bonds to be issued by retailer Philippine Seven Corp to the former foreign stockholders of its property unit, a bourse official said on Thursday.
Philippine Seven, the exclusive local holder of 7-Eleven franchise, is planning to list the warrants simultaneous with the initial public offering (IPO) of 71.4 million shares next month.
Under the proposal, former foreign investors of the firm's property unit can exercise the warrants under a 250 shares for one warrant ratio.
The holders of the warrants have the option to buy the shares within a period of five years.
Each of the warrant also has an attached bond with a face value of 382.45 pesos each. Philippine Seven has to pay an interest of four percent per year to the holder of the bond.

Philippine Seven said some 60,328 warrants will be issued to the Philippine American Life Insurance Co, 43,433 units to investment firm H&Q Ventures Philippines, 13,970 to Southland Corp, and 5,151 to Anglo-Philippines Corp.

Under Philippine laws, foreign investors cannot own shares of retail companies. The warrants will allow foreign investors to hold Philippine Seven shares should a law allowing foreign ownership in retail business is passed.
